The perimeter is the length of the closed curve $f$, which equals $\int_0^{2\pi} |f'(\theta)|\,d\theta$.

Differentiating term by term:

$$f'(\theta) = i e^{i\theta} + 2i e^{2i\theta} + i e^{3i\theta} = i e^{i\theta}\left(1 + 2e^{i\theta} + e^{2i\theta}\right) = i e^{i\theta}\left(1+e^{i\theta}\right)^2.$$

Taking magnitudes, $|i e^{i\theta}| = 1$, so

$$|f'(\theta)| = |1+e^{i\theta}|^2 = (1+\cos\theta)^2 + \sin^2\theta = 2 + 2\cos\theta.$$

Therefore

$$\text{Perimeter} = \int_0^{2\pi} (2+2\cos\theta)\,d\theta = 4\pi + 2[\sin\theta]_0^{2\pi} = 4\pi.$$

ANSWER: $4\pi$
